images.alt: Overview shows All systems running, one session and the remote September 12 server build.
System Performance identifies ARM Linux and the remote workspace.
Live Security Posture shows Standard sandbox, Interactive approval and control coverage counts.
The S3 upload command rule is on with a disabled switch and an organization-policy explanation.
Denied Commands lists credential, shell, destructive-command and publication rule categories.
The expanded IaC teardown category shows CDK destroy, Kubernetes namespace deletion, Pulumi destroy and Terraform destroy rules.
Denied Commands shows 112 built-in rules and the enabled custom pattern KIROCREW_DEMO_COMMAND_CONTROL_20260913.
Denied Commands shows an empty custom-deny list after the temporary marker was removed; 112 built-in rules remain listed.
The session approval menu lists Normal, Reads and Trust; Normal is selected and YOLO is absent.
The YOLO duration screen shows Interactive in its sidebar and a six-hour next-activation selection.
Governance Policy shows Policy v1, file source, startup-only refresh, cc sandbox floor and the configured policy lists.
Governance Policy states No enterprise policy in effect and describes standalone mode.
MCP Servers shows the enabled Crew-only aws-enforcement server with four tools.
The MCP manager shows one staged tool restriction and the Apply and Discard buttons.
Session options shows aws-enforcement started, zero of four tool specifications loaded, and read_allowed, crew_denied, mcp_denied and iam_denied listed as deferred tools.
The actual macOS client shows the expanded host notice identifying the automatic governance-policy block of crew_denied.
The expanded SEL audit logging row lists session-key surfaces including Background, CLI, Cron and Dashboard.
Kiro CLI is selected beside a GitHub sign-in card representing KAS identity.
Privacy shows Gateway metrics enabled and anonymous telemetry disabled.
Native Telemetry expands the MCP Tool Call Read Allowed session into four completed turns, with durations 12.3, 8.9, 14.2 and 17.7 seconds.
Native Telemetry expands the command-demonstration session into its one recorded turn and shows the aggregate runtime measurements.
Native Telemetry expands the anonymous-probe session into one recorded turn; the header shows 0 faults of 9 and throughput 23.
Demo Observability shows macOS client and EC2 server samples with freshness and service checks.
Collection logs show source labels, timestamps, event levels and All, Client and Server filters.
Demo Observability shows Current macOS and EC2 samples, local Gateway off, client 3.7% CPU and 967.1 MiB memory, and server 0.7% CPU with 12.6 GiB available.
Demo Observability shows expanded server process measurements and a Server-only collection log containing one First sample collected event at 10:31:23.
Actual native recording frame shows the public sensitive-path canary read returning ENOENT.
The native macOS client reports a protected-config write refusal; its file panel displays both 1 file changed and no changes.
The native IMDS TCP result reports EHOSTUNREACH, zero application bytes and no metadata request.
